name: AIDA (Attention, Interest, Desire, Action)
summary: A classic sales funnel: capture attention, build interest with relevant detail, create desire with benefits, then ask for action.
references: E. St. Elmo Lewis, advertising funnel model (1898)
Edward K. Strong, The Psychology of Selling (1925)
title_style: Benefit-led titles, under 10 words, speaking to the buyer.

sequence.purpose: Attention: a sharp line that stops the scroll.
Interest: connect to a real situation.
Interest: show how it works in brief.

pitfalls: Features dressed as desire; translate them into outcomes.
A soft or missing call to action.
Spending too long on attention before giving substance.

example.topic: A fictional smart plant waterer pitched to home buyers
outline: Your plants are thirsty while you are away
Holidays and busy weeks kill houseplants
Sensor, reservoir, app: set up in five minutes
Come home to green leaves, every time
Synthetic trial: 9 of 10 plants thrived for a month
